title: #53 Todd Wenning on Lessons from the Titans

reader_summary.headline: I'm your host, Eddie Palmingen, and with me in the studio is my friend and colleague, Niklas Savos.
reader_summary.overview: I'm your host, Eddie Palmingen, and with me in the studio is my friend and colleague, Niklas Savos. In today's episode, we will speak to an experienced investor who has selected a superb book to discuss with us. And this is a format we find interesting to mix with the pure author interviews that we're usually doing.

key_points.text: So the person we have invited this time is Todd Wenning, an American investor, and writer with a background, including Ensemble Capital, Motley Fool.
key_points.evidence_quote: So the person we have invited this time is Todd Wenning, an American investor, and writer with a background, including Ensemble Capital, Motley Fool, and Morning Star.

key_points.text: In episode five, we actually came across some of Todd's work, since he's a contributing author to the book Why Modes Matter.
key_points.evidence_quote: In episode five, we actually came across some of Todd's work, since he's a contributing author to the book Why Modes Matter.

key_points.text: The book for this episode is Lessons from the Titans, with the subtitle.
key_points.evidence_quote: The book for this episode is Lessons from the Titans, with the subtitle, what companies in the new economy can learn from the great industrial giants to drive sustainable success.

key_points.text: The book is written by Scott Davis, Carter Copeland, and Rob Vertheimer.
key_points.evidence_quote: The book is written by Scott Davis, Carter Copeland, and Rob Vertheimer.

thesis: The episode introduces Todd Wenning, an investor with experience at Vanguard, Motley Fool, and Morningstar, who discusses his career progression and interest in business history. The conversation highlights his current work with Ensemble Capital and his newsletter, which focuses on companies with economic moats led by thoughtful leaders.
